El disco de Poincaré no es solo un jugue: The Poincaré disc is not just a plaything for geometers. It is the model used to draw Escher's Circle Limit prints, in which identical fish seem to shrink towards the edge: they do not shrink, it is that distances are greater there. And it is the natural geometry of networks: the internet, social networks and neural connections have a structure far better represented in the hyperbolic plane than in the Euclidean one, because an exponential growth of neighbours with distance “fits” in it. There are routing and machine learning algorithms that work directly in hyperbolic coordinates.

Maryam Mirzakhani, an Iranian mathematician, devoted her career to hyperbolic surfaces: shapes in which, as in the disc of this topic, triangles add up to less than $180^\circ$. In 2014 she became the first woman to receive the Fields medal, the most prestigious prize in mathematics, for her work on the geometry and dynamics of these surfaces. She died in 2017, aged forty.
La historia de Bolyai tiene un final ama: Bolyai's story has a bitter ending worth telling. His father, Farkas, had spent years on the fifth postulate without success and begged him by letter not to follow that path: “I entreat you, leave it alone, fear it like sensual desire, because it can rob you of all your time, your health, your peace and all the happiness of your life”. János paid no heed and solved the problem. Farkas, proud, sent the work to his old friend Gauss, who replied that he could not praise it because to do so would be to praise himself: he had known it for thirty years.
